title: Wikipedia iOS app 8.0 on iOS 26
lede: The Wikimedia Foundation’s iPhone app, version 8.0.0, whose floating glass tab bar and search button bend the photo that scrolls under them.
summary: A third-party app with a floating glass tab bar that visibly refracts the content. 2026.
made: 2026 (release tag releases/8.0.0 dated April 13, 2026; screenshot April 19, 2026)

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons screenshot IOS App 8.0.0 Explore.png (1179 × 2556) by EvanTech10, with a 1:1 crop of the tab bar. Also looked at the companion IOS App 8.0.0 Article.png. Not stored.

styles.note: A non-Apple app that adopts the system material: content-first pages under a floating glass tab bar that refracts at its rim.

context: The app is open source under the MIT license. Its code calls Apple’s glassEffect API, for example in WMFHomeView.swift and WMFFindInPageView.swift. [GitHub: wikimedia/wikipedia-ios](https://github.com/wikimedia/wikipedia-ios).

Apple Developer: standard SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit controls and navigation elements “pick up the appearance and behavior of this material automatically”. [Apple Developer: Liquid Glass](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/liquid-glass).
observed: Dark mode. A “Today” feed with a serif featured-article card and a “Picture of the day” photo of a green and violet faceted glass dome.
At the top, the Wikipedia “W” sits in a separate dark glass circle on the left, and two icons share a dark glass capsule on the right. Neither is pinned to the screen edge.
At the bottom, a glass capsule holds four tabs (Explore, Places, Saved, Activity), and a separate glass circle holds the search icon. Both float over the photo.

In the 1:1 crop the straight frame lines of the dome curve into loops just inside the rims of the capsule and the circle, while the middle stays nearly undistorted. A thin bright line marks the rim. The selected tab sits in a lighter inner capsule.
The Article screenshot shows the same pattern: a back button, a “W” circle, and a three-icon capsule float over the lead image, and a toolbar capsule floats over the article text.
interpretation: Because the app uses system components, it shows the default behavior of the material that any developer gets, not an Apple marketing render.
borrow: Split navigation into a tab capsule and a separate search circle, so the most used action has its own target.

rights.statement: The Commons file is CC BY-SA 4.0 by EvanTech10, and the app code is MIT. It is kept as link only because the frame also shows Apple’s system interface and a picture of the day whose own license was not checked.
